rationale: The scheduled workflow already bounds both jobs with explicit timeouts (exhaustive 90 min, bench 30 min), so P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT's intent—preventing runaway job consumption with an explicit budget—is already satisfied; adding or tightening a timeout is unsupported because cold dependency installation plus the 5.8M-line exhaustive suite lacks representative cold-run history and a tighter limit risks false timeouts (pattern contraindication: valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit). Dependency fetching is already cached via setup-node cache: yarn, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated (an equivalent cache already exists). The schedule-level patterns P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE and P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE are ci_service-scoped rather than workflow_yaml changes and fail applicability: the exhaustive conformance/benchmarks are mandatory periodic checks that also fetch an external re2 binary (contraindicated for inactivity suppression), and the 3-consecutive-failure pause threshold is not met by the history. No matrix exists for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, and change-based filtering/selection would reduce required conformance coverage. Preserving intended build and test coverage therefore warrants no workflow change.
